evidence.note: Not confirmed. A 1931 film is public domain only if it lacked a notice or its renewal was missed. I searched the first 100,000 characters of the 1959 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volume (about 800,000 characters in total) and found no renewal for The Front Page. That is partial coverage, not a full check. The 1958 and 1960 volumes and the Copyright Office catalog were not searched.

editorial:
The Front Page (1931) is Lewis Milestone's film of the Ben Hecht and Charles MacArthur play. Howard Hughes produced it. Adolphe Menjou plays the editor, who uses every tactic to keep his star reporter, played by Pat O'Brien, from quitting journalism to marry. The film earned three Academy Award nominations. Many Internet Archive copies circulate, and that is why creators ask about it.

The rights trap is that a film from 1931 is not free by default. The 1931 print is free only if its renewal was missed, and this dossier has not confirmed that. Only part of one 1959 renewal volume was read, and no renewal turned up in that part. The story layer also needs the play's own publication and renewal history checked. Until those checks are done, treat reuse as unverified rather than cleared.
faq: Is the 1931 Front Page free to reuse?

Not confirmed. Its status depends on whether the 1931 film's copyright was renewed in its 28th year, around 1958 to 1960. The partial search found no renewal, but the check is incomplete. Search the full Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes before relying on it.
Does the Internet Archive listing prove the film is free?
No. Uploaders label items as public domain without proof. The Archive hosts several copies of this film, but a listing is not a copyright record.
